newsitem.title: UK: Tumbling FTSE futures shake UK blue chip stocks.
newsitem.headline: Tumbling FTSE futures shake UK blue chip stocks.

text.p: UK stocks had a turbulent session on Monday as both technical and fundamental concerns battered sentiment in the futures market and sent the September FTSE futures contract spiralling downwards.
In its first full day of trade as the lead contract, the September future plunged to a 70-point discount to the cash market soon after trade began.

"All the sellers came in at once this morning and we got completely smacked," said one futures trader. "It was just like the 1987 crash where things were marked down, marked down, marked down...and there was no bid."
Fair value for the contract was a premium of around 30 points to the cash market, traders said. The FTSE 100 index was down 43 points at 4,550.9 by 1044 GMT.
As the futures market sunk, UK blue-chips followed suit. The September future fell to a low of 4,525.0 whilst the FTSE 100 was dragged to a low of 4,547.0 down some 46 points from Friday's close.
Derivatives specialists said persistent fears that the government would cut the tax credit on dividend payments in the July 2 Budget was harming sentiment.
A technical overhang of stock following Friday's options and futures expiry was also dampening the mood.
"There is suddenly a complete lack of buyers around," said one senior derivatives specialist.
"The future opened and there was literally not one bid out there, so it was continually offered down and only at the 4,525 level did we find some buyers again," he added.
Traders said the "double whammy" of futures and options expiry last Friday had resulted in more stock coming into the market, which had previously been short.
"Market makers who had previously been short have now found themselves long and the market is very messy," a trader said.
"The market has clearly broken its uptrend and we left a very nasty week behind us."
The FTSE 100 index fell every day last week for a net 190 point loss over the five sessions.
